title: R&B audiences wanted singing, not jazz
summary: At a Wilmington dance the crowd waited outside for Ray Charles, so Thomas tells him his band must play R&B.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: He used to play dances... I was down at a dance in Wilmington, Delaware, he was playing... And the band used to play an hour before he came on. And the guys was playin', and nobody was going in the hall! All the people were standing outside waiting. So I just looked at it, and I said to myself... In Rhythm-and-Blues in those days, the audiences didn't (?) Jazz. Jazz was something they didn't dig! And all these guys he had in his band were Jazz musicians. They was just playin' their thing. They weren't playin' nothin' Rhythm-and-Blues.

So I've always been outspoken of what I think. So I came back off and told them... I said, "Ray Charles has got to sing his format. He's got to start playing...the band has got to start playing the things that the R&B people want to come in and see. Because they ain't interested in Jazz." They're ain't gonna do it. Because here are about five hundred people standing outside, and when he hit the stage, they broke the doors down -- you couldn't hardly get the people in there, the people were coming in so heavy. And they had come to hear Ray Charles sing.
But the new group of Rhythm-and-Blues artists had this situation where the band would play the first hour, and then they would come on. You know, in our days, Calloway hit with us.
